question: Measure, rather than infer, the non-top-50 part of the numerator: extend mission_daf_share_recipient_revenue.py to every DAFRC panel sponsor whose FY2023-FY2024 return itemises Schedule I (netpayout990 cache holds the returns; the full line cache would need the same GivingTuesday-mirror re-read used for the top 50), then recompute the sampled recipients' shares and compare with the 1/0.673 scaling
conclusion_affected: Scaled DAF-share estimates (10.2% pooled, 8.8% median) rest on the assumption that the other 32.7% of netted FY2024 DAF grants reach recipients in top-50 proportions
proposed_by: b40n12-02 agent (DAF share of recipient revenue)
rationale: Community-foundation and small-sponsor grants are likely more local and smaller-recipient-weighted than national-sponsor grants, so uniform scaling may understate small-org shares and overstate large-org shares

question: Classify pass-through intermediaries among DAF recipients (fiscal sponsors, donor collaboratives and re-granting public charities, e.g. New Venture Fund, Hopewell Fund, Blue Meridian Partners, Navigation Charitable Fund, The 85 Fund) using Schedule I outbound grants as a share of their own expenses, and re-run the share excluding them
conclusion_affected: Pooled DAF share (6.9% unscaled) vs the 5.9% produced by a crude name/NTEE-T exclusion; whether DAF money to operating charities is overstated by re-granting vehicles
proposed_by: b40n12-02 agent (DAF share of recipient revenue)
rationale: The 400-EIN certainty stratum is led by re-granting intermediaries with DAF shares of 34-100%; the current sensitivity uses names only (FOUNDATION/FUND/TRUST) and drops operating charities such as Environmental Defense Fund

question: Move the denominator toward Chariot's 'individual giving' basis: parse Form 990 Part VIII lines 1a-1f (federated campaigns, membership dues, fundraising events, related organisations, government grants, all other) and Schedule A Part II/III public-support lines for the sampled recipients, and report DAF share of line 1f and of 1h less 1a, 1d and 1e
conclusion_affected: Gap between the independent pooled share (6.9% of 1h; 10.1% of 1h-1e) and Chariot's 'nearly 13%' of total giving / 4-24% of individual revenue
proposed_by: b40n12-02 agent (DAF share of recipient revenue)
rationale: Line 1h mixes foundation, corporate, federated and related-organisation money with individual gifts; the 1h-1e basis already raises the pooled share by about half, and Chariot's denominator definition is gated (P-B40N12-01)

question: Raise precision where the sample is thin: draw a supplementary seeded sample of 150 EINs each for no-NTEE <$1m (4 in-scope respondents of 40) and religion <$1m (15 of 40), and a full census of the 4,458 frame recipients with BMF revenue >= $25m (about 9,000 returns, under 10 minutes with the streamed reader)
conclusion_affected: Religion and small-org medians (13.4%, CI 4.4-16.6%; <$1m band 10.1%) and the size gradient
proposed_by: b40n12-02 agent (DAF share of recipient revenue)
rationale: Most sampled EINs in these strata have no FY2023-24 990/990-EZ (churches, 990-N filers), so each in-scope respondent carries a weight of several hundred to several thousand

question: Reduce timing noise and add a trend: extend the numerator and denominator to FY2021-FY2025 (three- or four-year pooled windows), to test whether the DAF share of recipient contributions rose as Chariot's '+75% median DAF revenue growth' implies, and whether pledge accrual explains the 2.8% of recipients with shares above 100%
conclusion_affected: Trend statements on nonprofit-side DAF growth; credibility of recipient-level shares
proposed_by: b40n12-02 agent (DAF share of recipient revenue)
rationale: Sponsor grants are cash paid in the sponsor's fiscal year, while recipients book contributions on an accrual (pledge) basis in their own fiscal year; two-year pooling still leaves 2.8% (weighted) of in-scope recipients above 100%
